verdict.rationale: Tailscale provides transparent IP-level connectivity that lets standard SSH-based tools work as if on a LAN, and evidence shows SSH access to remote boxes works well (tailscale-docs-7, tailscale-comm-1) plus a dedicated 'Tailscale SSH' feature for managing SSH connections (tailscale-docs-26). However, none of the evidence explicitly confirms scp/sftp usage with a developer's own configured SSH keys — Tailscale SSH appears to manage its own auth rather than passing through user keys, and the only file-transfer feature documented (Taildrop, tailscale-docs-23) is for personal device-to-device transfer, not scp/sftp. missing for 10: explicit documentation or hands-on confirmation of scp/sftp working with user-configured SSH keys over Tailscale, detail on whether Tailscale SSH interferes with standard key-based auth.
